title: Fifth increment of the Goal Gravity loop: explicit, evidence-preserving torn-tail recovery of the Evidence Ledger (provenance/recovery.py) as the residual deficit behind entry-gate proof P2
problem: A process killed inside an EvidenceLedger append leaves a partial final line; EvidenceLedger refuses to open it (fail-closed, correct), so the institution's history cannot be reopened and entry-gate proof P2 (interruption and autonomous recovery: reopen canonical history, preserve uncertainty, no duplicate consequence) cannot pass with any supervisor. The first four increments characterized the gap by test and listed it as unrepaired. The only way forward was a person editing the canonical ledger by hand, which is unaccountable and can silently drop an acknowledged record (for example a grant_dispatch claim, after which a restarted body could dispatch the same route again).
founder_intent_refs: 2026-11-13 founder message: Resume and Follow the repository's own entry instructions
baseline: Draft PR #160 at 637b976 (fourth increment after review fixes; 794 tests, CI green): a torn final ledger line refuses to load and nothing repairs it; the process-kill tests cover SIGKILL after dispatch and before the gate but not inside an append.

alternatives.name: Explicit recovery module with named risks (selected)
alternatives.description: provenance/recovery.py: under the writer lock, verify the prefix, accept only a tail one interrupted append can leave, require named acknowledgment of unanchored/complete_record/stop_record, copy the torn bytes atomically beside the ledger, truncate, chain a ledger.torn_tail_quarantined event; never re-admit the torn record; never automatic.
advantages: Evidence is preserved byte for byte and the repair is itself chained evidence
The ambiguity a byte check cannot resolve is surfaced as named risks instead of hidden in a mode
No change to EvidenceLedger or to any contract; organs pinning the boundary archive are unaffected
Mirrors mature WAL practice (etcd wal.Repair backup-then-truncate) with an evidence-grade record
disadvantages: Needs a caller: P2 stays incomplete until a supervisor (G5) exists
An operator can acknowledge a risk carelessly; the module records the acknowledgment but cannot judge it
Adds about 350 lines to the provenance boundary package

alternatives.name: Tolerant load inside EvidenceLedger (RocksDB kTolerateCorruptedTailRecords style)
alternatives.description: EvidenceLedger._load drops an incomplete trailing record automatically on open.
disadvantages: Silent loss in every organ that pins the boundary package
RocksDB's own source notes the mode cannot tell a torn tail from real corruption
alternatives.revival_evidence: A founder ruling that silent tolerance is acceptable for a named ledger class

alternatives.name: Self-delimiting framing (length and checksum prefix, hash_version 3)
alternatives.description: Change the record framing so torn writes are detectable by construction.
advantages: Torn writes detectable without parsing heuristics
disadvantages: Does not remove the acknowledged-then-damaged ambiguity
alternatives.revival_evidence: Torn tails recur in a live deployment, or the ledger owner schedules a format migration for other reasons

alternatives.name: Atomic per-record writes (temporary file plus rename, or one file per record)
alternatives.description: Make each append atomic at the filesystem level.
disadvantages: O(n) rewrite per append or a new storage layout
alternatives.revival_evidence: A storage-layer redesign for other reasons

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Opening a torn ledger keeps failing closed forever; P2 cannot pass; the de facto repair is a hand edit of the canonical ledger with no record of who removed what.
advantages: Zero risk of a repair bug
disadvantages: A crash at the worst moment ends the institution's history until a person edits it by hand
Hand edits can drop an acknowledged dispatch claim and allow a duplicate consequence
Leaves the Goal Gravity directive's restart-continuity requirement with no mechanism

roles.position: The founder asked for restart continuity without duplicate consequence; the honest current form is an accountable repair plus an end-to-end kill test, with P2 explicitly left open until a supervisor exists.
material_concerns: Do not describe this as autonomous recovery or as P2 passing
Keep the destination (24/7 continuity) visible in the blocked table

roles.position: Keep EvidenceLedger untouched and put the repair beside it; the lock, verification and recording must be one critical section; naming files by prior head and digest makes every incident distinct.
material_concerns: The path-keyed lock is a ledger-level defect that recovery can only partially guard against

roles.position: The first design let cut-back acknowledged records pass as partial and released the lock before recording; both were reproduced and fixed, and the replay found a stale-checkpoint hole that is now closed. The residual danger is a supervisor that acknowledges every risk unattended.
material_concerns: Named risks become boilerplate if a supervisor passes them by default
A 40-byte cut of an acknowledged record is accepted when 'unanchored' is acknowledged (by design, recorded)

roles.position: One function, standard library only, idempotent and crash-safe at every step; stray .tmp files are the only residue. Alias-proof locking should move into EvidenceLedger.
material_concerns: Quarantine files accumulate beside the ledger and need a retention rule
Bind mounts of the ledger file remain an undetectable alias

roles.position: Every claim the event makes is now conditional on what was proven; everything remains synthetic and no supervisor has used it.
material_concerns: No real crash on a live ledger has been recovered
Evidence tier must stay at UNIT/INTEGRATION-TESTED

evidence.claim: Recovery repairs a ledger torn by a real SIGKILL inside the dispatch-claim append without loss, admission or re-dispatch
evidence.finding: torn line classified partial/grant_dispatch, quarantined byte-for-byte; chain verifies; no grant_dispatch survives; intervention stays attempted; no second dispatch; reconcile reports unresolved

evidence.claim: Every confirmed review finding is fixed
evidence.finding: 26 reviewer probes replayed against the fixed tree: 19 complete with no reproduction, 7 end in a deliberate refusal

evidence.claim: The full suite passes with the increment
Backup-then-truncate of a torn WAL tail is established practice, and tolerant modes cannot distinguish torn tails from corruption
evidence.finding: etcd wal.Repair truncates a last file ending in ErrUnexpectedEOF after a .broken copy; RocksDB documents kTolerateCorruptedTailRecords' ambiguity and defaults to point-in-time recovery

counterevidence.claim: An acknowledged record can still be dropped
counterevidence.finding: A 40-byte cut of an acknowledged grant_dispatch is accepted when the caller acknowledges 'unanchored'; the event records the acknowledgment and says an acknowledged record cut back cannot be excluded. Inherent to byte-level evidence without a fresh checkpoint.
No supervisor restarts the process; recovery is called by tests only

pass_1.intended_outcome: A crash at the worst moment does not end the institution's history: an accountable call reopens it, preserves the torn bytes and the uncertainty they carry, records the repair in the chain, and the loop never produces the same consequence twice.

advantages.statement: Torn bytes are preserved and the repair is chained
advantages.amplified_value: Turns a crash into evidence the institution can audit later; reverses into a liability only if quarantine files are deleted, which nothing does
Every recovery records which risks its caller accepted, so a later audit can find the ones that relied on 'unanchored'; reverses if a supervisor acknowledges everything by default
Organs can adopt it by re-pinning without migration; the ledger owner keeps the format decision

advantages.statement: End-to-end kill test on the dispatch claim
advantages.amplified_value: The most dangerous crash point for duplicate consequences is exercised with a real SIGKILL; becomes the regression gate for any future supervisor

disadvantages.statement: P2 remains incomplete without a supervisor
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Stated in the ADR, the ledger entry, docs and PR; the supervisor's acknowledgment policy is named as part of the G5 decision

disadvantages.statement: A careless caller can acknowledge a risk and drop an acknowledged record
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Acknowledgments are recorded in the sidecar and the chained event; the disposition text says what could not be excluded; expected_head narrows the case

disadvantages.statement: The writer lock is keyed on the path, so aliases can hide a live writer
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Recovery refuses symlinks and hard-linked files; the root cause is referred to the ledger owner

disadvantages.statement: Quarantine and scratch files accumulate beside the ledger
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Names are distinct and ignored unless they match the full pattern; a retention rule is left to the operator
The classifier accepts only exact prefixes of the next record's serialization or NULs and refuses everything else; every cut offset of real records is covered by tests

comparisons.baseline: Fail-closed forever; hand edits as the de facto repair
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Tolerant load in EvidenceLedger: simpler, but silent and contract-changing
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Self-delimiting framing with checksums: stronger detection, shared migration, same acknowledged-then-damaged ambiguity

pass_2.attack_summary: An independent review attacked the first design on three lenses and reproduced 13 real defects (partial-bypass of the complete-record guard, a lock gap, non-atomic copies, identical-tear collisions, glob over-match, symlink alias, stale proof, misattribution); the replay of its probes found a fourth class (a stale checkpoint excusing a complete record). A second review of the final tree attacked the classifier, crash safety and evidence honesty again.

new_weaknesses.statement: A supervisor could pass every risk name by default, making acknowledgment boilerplate
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The module cannot prevent it; the G5 decision must name who may acknowledge which risk, and the event records each acknowledgment for audit

new_weaknesses.statement: A crash mid-copy leaves .tmp scratch files
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: They never match the quarantine pattern and never block recovery or get chained

new_weaknesses.statement: Three risk names and four classifications are more than an operator expects
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Refusal messages name each missing risk with one sentence of why; the README and ADR define them

new_weaknesses.statement: Correctness depends on EvidenceLedger's serialization staying ASCII JSON with fixed field order
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: The classifier's prefix and closing-field constants mirror the ledger; a format change makes recovery refuse, not accept, and the tests sweep real serialized records

new_weaknesses.statement: Truncation removes bytes from the canonical file
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Bytes are copied durably before truncation and the copy's digest is in the chained event; a quarantined line can always be inspected

Inherent to byte-level evidence without a fresh checkpoint; recorded per recovery
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: First recovery on a live ledger

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The root fix belongs in EvidenceLedger, which organs pin

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: More than a handful of quarantine files on any ledger

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Strict prefix classifier with refusal by default; offset sweeps in tests

pass_2.final_design: recover_torn_tail under one held lock: refuse aliases and live writers; verify the prefix; accept only a prefix of the next record or NULs; require named acknowledgment of unanchored (no expected_head), complete_record (any complete tail, anchored or not) and stop_record; copy atomically beside the ledger; truncate; chain one event per quarantine file with conditional disposition text; never re-admit; never automatic.

residual_risks.risk: Unattended acknowledgment by a future supervisor
residual_risks.mitigation: Named in the G5 decision; each acknowledgment chained

residual_risks.risk: Alias of the ledger file through a bind mount or a writer in another mount namespace
residual_risks.mitigation: Symlinks and hard links refused; root fix referred

residual_risks.risk: Recovery mistaken for proof that nothing was lost
residual_risks.mitigation: Disposition text is conditional; ADR and docs state the limits
residual_risks.review_trigger: First recovery on a live ledger

dissent.handling: Recorded, not resolved; the increment proceeds as a reversible experiment on the draft with each dissent's threshold named.

entries.position: Unattended recovery should never acknowledge 'unanchored' or 'complete_record'
entries.rationale: Those are exactly the cases where an acknowledged record can be lost; a machine accepting them for the founder converts evidence loss into policy
entries.evidence_threshold: The G5 decision either keeps these acknowledgments human-only or supplies a fresh per-append checkpoint that makes expected_head meaningful

entries.position: The alias problem should be fixed in EvidenceLedger now, not referred
entries.rationale: Two writers on one file through aliases can fork the ledger outside recovery too
entries.evidence_threshold: A ledger-owner change that locks the ledger file's own descriptor, released with a boundary-package version organs re-pin

migration_plan: Additive module and tests on draft PR #160's branch; no change to EvidenceLedger, contracts, manifests or organs; organs pin the boundary archive and are unaffected until they re-pin.

kill_criteria: Any recovery drops an acknowledged record without a named risk that admits it
A truncation is ever left without its chained event once the call returns
A torn record is ever admitted to the chain
Recovery is ever cited as authority to act
The founder rules that ledger repair must be impossible rather than explicit
review_trigger: Founder review of draft PR #160; G5 supervisor selection; the first recovery of a live ledger; any change to EvidenceLedger serialization
